text: With the pilot scoped and the identity sprawl mapped, Mara writes down one named target architecture — the document every remaining technical lesson in this chapter builds a piece of.

It has three pillars. A segmented OT and IT boundary that replaces the current flat network with an explicit allow-list, where no traffic reaches SCADA unless a specific rule permits it. A consolidated identity view, federating AWS IAM Identity Center to Entra ID so there's one identity plane instead of two disconnected ones. And an automated, Python-built inventory that keeps the answer to who has access always current and queryable, instead of a manual, stale snapshot.

These three pillars are sequenced, not parallel. Segmentation makes the boundary worth consolidating identity around. The consolidated identity view gives the automation one coherent source to query instead of automating a mess faster. And the automation is what makes the whole architecture provable — the artifact that will later let Mara, a compliance audit, and the SIEM each independently check whether reality matches the design.
That third point matters more than it looks like right now. Next lesson starts building pillar one: the actual network segmentation plan for Riverbend's OT and SCADA boundary.
